# Testfunction index

<!-- Generated by `adare test catalog --markdown-dir`; do not edit by hand. -->

One line per testfunction: `name` [asserts · formats] use for. Prefer `adare test search "<goal>"`;
read `catalog/<collection>.md` (or `adare test info <name>`) for parameters, outcomes, limits and
examples, and `features.md` (or `adare test feature <id>`) for shared syntax.

**Assertion kinds:** `exists` a file, folder, key, row, element or entry is present, `absent` something is gone or was never written (a negative test, INCONCLUSIVE without proof of the act), `value` a value equals or matches an expected value (exact, regex, placeholder), `count` how many times something occurs or how many items there are, `order` a number or point in time is greater, less or within a tolerance of another, `sequence` lines or records occur in a given order (one after the other, others in between allowed), `compare` two files, sheets or values of one file are compared with each other, `content` the raw content or bytes of a file (contains, equals, regex, hash, size), `metadata` file system metadata (timestamps, permissions, owner), `state` live state of the guest system (service, process, user, registry), `ui` what is visible on the screen


## Binary (`catalog/binary.md`)

- `binary.pair_count` [count, absent · binary] asserting a metadata element is absent from a key/value string table (`expected_count: 0`) or occurs a given number of times.
- `binary.pair_value_matches` [value · binary] "metadata element X has value Y" in a binary container that stores its metadata as alternating key and value strings (`key\0value\0key\0value\0`), e.g. in a block that the file's last bytes point to.
- `binary.pattern_count` [count, absent · binary] counting records, markers or values inside one part of a binary file (only the metadata block a trailer points to, the records after a header); a regex over raw bytes; asserting a value is gone from that part: …
- `binary.struct_value_matches` [value, order · binary] a field of a binary container no parser knows: a counter, flag, size or timestamp in a header, a record of an index file, a string in a metadata block that the file's last bytes point to. `offset` follows pointers …

## CSV (`catalog/csv.md`)

- `csv.compare_files` [compare · csv] diffing a produced CSV against a reference CSV available on the same machine.
- `csv.compare_rows` [compare, value · csv] asserting a whole (small) CSV export.
- `csv.contains_line` [exists · csv] checking a tool's CSV output (e.g. a timeline) contains a specific record.
- `csv.row_count` [count, absent · csv] asserting how often a record occurs (exactly one row for a file); absence of a row: `expected_count: 0` (or `expect_to_fail: true` on csv.contains_line).

## Excel (`catalog/excel.md`)

- `excel.cell_value_matches` [value, order · excel] asserting one value a user typed or a formula result saved in a workbook.
- `excel.compare_files` [compare · excel] whole-workbook comparison.
- `excel.compare_rows` [compare, value · excel] asserting sheet contents.
- `excel.compare_sheets` [compare · excel] comparing two sheets of the same or different workbooks.
- `excel.contains_row` [exists · excel] checking a record exists anywhere in a sheet.
- `excel.row_count` [count, absent · excel] asserting how often a record occurs (exactly one row for an item); absence of a row: `expected_count: 0` (or `expect_to_fail: true` on excel.contains_row).
- `excel.sheet_exists` [exists · excel] checking a GUI action added/renamed a worksheet.
- `excel.validate_columns` [value · excel] verifying a sheet's column layout/schema.

## Image (`catalog/image.md`)

- `image.dimensions_match` [value · image] checking an exported, resized or cropped image, or a generated thumbnail.
- `image.exif_value_count` [count, absent · image] absence: `expected_count: 0` asserts the tag was not written (or stripped, e.g. location data removed on export).
- `image.exif_value_matches` [exists, value, order · image] camera, time and location metadata written into photos (JPEG, PNG eXIf, TIFF, WebP).
- `image.png_text_count` [count, absent · image] duplicate keywords and absence: `expected_count: 0` asserts no such chunk (or none with that text).
- `image.png_text_matches` [exists, value · image] metadata an application embeds in saved images (software, source, comment).

## INI (`catalog/ini.md`)

- `ini.contains_key` [exists · ini] checking a setting was written, whatever its value.
- `ini.section_exists` [exists · ini] checking a settings file gained a section.
- `ini.value_count` [count, absent · ini] duplicate keys (lists written as repeated keys) and absence: `expected_count: 0` asserts the key (or the key with that value) is not in the section.
- `ini.value_matches` [value, order · ini] asserting a setting's value.

## JSON (`catalog/json.md`)

- `json.array_contains` [value · json] checking that a list in a JSON file includes an entry.
- `json.contains_key` [exists · json] checking a settings/config file gained a key.
- `json.value_count` [count, absent · json] counting entries (e.g. exactly 3 bookmarks with a given tag) and asserting absence: `expected_count: 0` without `expected_value` passes when the key path selects nothing, with `expected_value` when no value …
- `json.value_matches` [value, order · json] asserting a setting/field value.
- `json.values_compare` [order, compare · json] relations inside one file (or between two, `other_dst`): a last-saved value later than the first-opened one, two timestamps within a few seconds of each other, a counter one above another (`comparison_type: equals` …

## JSONL (`catalog/jsonl.md`)

- `jsonl.line_count` [count, absent · jsonl] asserting how many records/events were written (e.g. exactly 3 deletions); absence: `expected_count: 0`.
- `jsonl.line_matches` [exists, value · jsonl] event logs / NDJSON exports (e.g. "a line with type=login and user=alice exists").
- `jsonl.lines_in_order` [sequence, value · jsonl] the order of events in an event log or NDJSON export (a login, then a download, then a deletion of the same file); records in between are ignored.
- `jsonl.value_in_any_line` [exists, value, order · jsonl] a single-field check across a log; for multi-field conditions use jsonl.line_matches.

## Linux (`catalog/linux.md`)

- `linux.log_entry_exists` [content, exists · text, system] checking an action left a trace in a plain-text log (syslog, auth.log, app logs; not the binary journal).
- `linux.process_running` [state, count · system] checking an application/daemon is (still) running after an action.
- `linux.system_service_status` [state, value · system] checking a systemd unit was started/stopped by an action.
- `linux.user_exists` [state, exists · system] verifying an account was created by an installer or admin action.

- `plist.contains_key` [exists · plist] checking that a preferences/settings plist gained a key.
- `plist.value_count` [count, absent · plist] counting entries (`recent[*]`) and asserting absence: `expected_count: 0` passes when the key path selects nothing (or nothing matches `expected_value`), while a missing or invalid file is still an error.

- `sqlite.free_space_pattern_count` [count, absent, content · sqlite] asserting that a deleted record is still recoverable from the database file (`comparison_type: greater_equal`, `expected_count: 1`) while a query no longer returns it (sqlite.row_count with `expected_count: 0`), …
- `sqlite.query_result` [exists, absent, value, count · sqlite] asserting that a row was written, changed or removed; which rows exist only in the write-ahead log, not yet checkpointed into the main file (`view: wal_added`), or are still in the main file but deleted or changed in …
- `sqlite.row_count` [count, exists, absent · sqlite] asserting how many records an action left behind (exactly one history entry for a URL); asserting a record is gone: `expected_count: 0`; asserting a row is only in the write-ahead log, not yet checkpointed into the …
- `sqlite.values_compare` [compare, order · sqlite] one check for "the write-ahead log adds exactly one row": `SELECT count(*)` on `view: current` equal to `other_view: main_file` with `offset: 1`; how a value changed between two transactions in the WAL (``view: …
- `sqlite.wal_frame_count` [count, absent · sqlite] asserting that changes are still in the WAL, not yet checkpointed into the main file (`frames: valid` greater than 0), how many transactions the WAL holds (`frames: commits`), or that a checkpoint emptied it …

## Standard (`catalog/standard.md`)

- `standard.dir_content` [exists · directory] checking a folder contains expected files/subfolders.
- `standard.dir_does_not_exist` [absent · directory] verifying a folder was removed or never created.
- `standard.dir_exists` [exists · directory] verifying an install/extract step created a folder.
- `standard.file_content_contains` [content · text, file] checking a value/marker was written into a file.
- `standard.file_content_equals` [content, value · text] exact output checks, e.g. a tool's exit code or a saved text document.
- `standard.file_content_matches_regex` [content · text] loose content checks (a value appears, a line has a given shape).
- `standard.file_count` [count, exists, absent · file, directory] how many files an application wrote (exactly 3 logs, at least one export) and absence of a whole group of files: `expected_count: 0`.
- `standard.file_does_not_exist` [absent · file] verifying a file was deleted or never written.
- `standard.file_exists` [exists · file] verifying a GUI action created/saved a file.
- `standard.file_hash_matches` [content · file] verifying a file is byte-identical to a known artifact.
- `standard.file_permissions` [metadata · file, directory] Unix mode/ownership checks after chmod/chown or a file save.
- `standard.file_size` [content · file] checking a file is empty (`expected_size: 0`), non-empty (`greater` 0) or grew/shrank past a threshold.
- `standard.file_timestamps` [metadata, order · file] MACB timestamp assertions (modified recently, accessed after an action, ...).

## Visual (`catalog/visual.md`)

- `visual.count_equals` [ui, count, absent · screen] counting visible items (e.g. 3 files on the desktop).
- `visual.count_max` [ui, count, absent · screen] "no more than N items visible"; `max: 0` behaves like visual.not_exists.
- `visual.count_min` [ui, count · screen] "at least N items visible".
- `visual.exists` [ui, exists · screen] confirming a GUI state (dialog shown, file icon on the desktop).
- `visual.not_exists` [ui, absent · screen] confirming a dialog closed or an item disappeared.

## Windows (`catalog/windows.md`)

- `windows.registry_key_exists` [state, exists · registry] checking an install/config action created a key.
- `windows.registry_value_matches` [state, value · registry] asserting a setting/MRU value written by an application.

- `xml.xpath_result_matches` [value, exists · xml] typed checks on the first matched element.
